story: Alex slammed the door behind him, the sound echoing through the quiet apartment. His hands trembled as he grabbed a mug from the cabinet, then hurled it against the wall, ceramic shattering like his patience. He paced, jaw clenched so tight his teeth ached, heat rising in his chest until his vision blurred. The silence that followed felt too loud, so he turned up the music, letting the bass thump like a heartbeat of protest. He couldn’t sit still, couldn’t think straight, just kept moving, fueled by a fire he couldn’t name.

Alex slammed the car door harder than necessary, the sound echoing through the empty parking lot. His jaw clenched as he stared at the crumpled note still in his hand, the ink smudged from his grip. He walked past the office window, catching a glimpse of the team huddled in a circle, laughing. His fingers curled into his palm, nails digging into his skin. He didn’t go in. Instead, he turned toward the exit, breathing fast, and pulled out his phone, scrolling for someone—anyone—to talk to.

Alex slammed the car door harder than necessary, the sound echoing through the empty parking lot. His hands trembled around the steering wheel as he stared at the message still glowing on his phone. The air inside the car felt thick, like it wasn’t moving at all, and his chest tightened with every shallow breath. He gripped the wheel tighter, knuckles white, and imagined pressing the gas instead of the brake. The engine idled, steady and unbothered, while he counted to ten in a voice he barely recognized.
